original_title: Real-World Outcomes of [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 in the French Early-Access Program for Patients with Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
title: Lu-177-PSMA-617, this time outside a trial
blurb: Real-world outcomes from France's early-access program for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, the messier patient population trials usually screen out. More useful than another VISION subgroup slice.

original_title: μMap-uAA: Photocatalytic proximity labeling targeted with single-residue precision
title: Putting the photocatalyst on one exact residue
blurb: μMap-uAA installs a tetrazine-quenched iridium photocatalyst at a genetically defined site via unnatural amino acid incorporation, so labeling fires from that one covalent point instead of drifting from wherever a tag happened to land. Applied to GPCRs, it maps interaction networks across receptor domains with both spatial and time resolution.

original_title: Conformation‐Guided Disulfide Pairing Enables Efficient Folding of Disulfide‐Rich Peptides
title: Folding disulfide-rich peptides by picking which bond forms first
blurb: A '1+2' strategy for peptides with three or more disulfide bonds: let one folding-promoting disulfide form first to pre-organize the native-like shape, then close the rest. Aimed straight at the misfolding and kinetic traps you get when all the bonds are left to form at once.

original_title: Triazine Linchpins for Selective Lys-Lys Stapling of Unprotected Peptides
title: Stapling two lysines together without touching cysteine
blurb: A 2,4-dichloro-1,3,5-triazine linchpin crosslinks lysine side-chain amines into macrocyclic peptides, tolerant of His, Trp, Arg, Tyr, Ser, Thr, and both free termini. The selling point is specifically that it leaves cysteine alone, unlike most stapling chemistry that competes for it.

original_title: Disulfide-crosslinked triblock polyampholyte vesicles as a reducible platform for polyplex-based nucleic acid delivery.
title: Vesicles that fall apart on cue for nucleic acid delivery
blurb: Triblock polyampholyte vesicles held together by disulfide crosslinks, built as a polyplex platform that's designed to disassemble in a reducing environment. Details are thin beyond that.

original_title: Electricity‐Driven Radical Carbonyl Catalysis for Asymmetric Synthesis of α ‐Tertiary Amino Esters
title: Running asymmetric catalysis on electrons instead of a chiral reagent
blurb: Electrochemistry paired with asymmetric organocatalysis to make α-tertiary amino esters with enantiocontrol. Stereocontrol under electrochemical conditions is a genuinely hard combination, since the polar environment and short-lived radical intermediates tend to wreck the noncovalent interactions doing the selecting, which is why the authors are making a point of it working at all.

original_title: Parameterizable salivary gland model for small-scale Monte Carlo radiopharmaceutical therapy dosimetry: evaluation of mouse and human model.
title: A Monte Carlo salivary gland model you can actually dial in
blurb: A parameterizable dosimetry model for radiopharmaceutical therapy's usual sore spot, the salivary glands, checked against both mouse and human geometries. Methods paper, not outcomes data.

original_title: Hematologic Consequences of Radiopharmaceutical Therapy: From Clonal Hematopoiesis to Therapy-Related Myeloid Neoplasms
title: What radiopharmaceutical therapy does to your bone marrow, eventually
blurb: A review tracing radiopharmaceutical therapy's hematologic toll from clonal hematopoiesis up through frank therapy-related myeloid neoplasms. The kind of downstream risk that only shows up once enough patients have racked up enough follow-up time.

original_title: Analysis of outcome in patients with different primary localisation of neuroendocrine tumors after PRRT. 10 years single institution experience.
title: Ten years of PRRT outcomes, sorted by where the tumor started
blurb: A single-institution look at neuroendocrine tumor patients after PRRT, broken down by primary tumor site. Single-center and retrospective, so it's a hypothesis generator more than a verdict.

original_title: Recent Advances in Stability-Indicating Chromatographic Methods for Simultaneous Quantitative Analysis of Combination Drug Products: Principles, Method Development Strategies, Validation, And Regulatory Perspectives
title: Stability-indicating methods for FDC drugs, all in one review
blurb: A roundup of RP-HPLC, UHPLC, UPLC, HPTLC, and LC approaches for quantifying several APIs at once in fixed-dose combination pills while tracking their degradation products and impurities. Covers method development strategy, validation, and what regulators expect to see. It's a review, not a new method, so there's no result here to argue with.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

original_title: A Tetrazine–Metal–Polyphenol Nanoprobe for Single-Tube Multimodal Sulfide Analysis
title: One tube, three separate ways to catch sulfide
blurb: A tetrazine-metal-polyphenol nanoprobe (RhB@Tz-MPN) reads sulfide three ways in the same tube: a UV-vis blue shift for a fast screen, fluorescence recovery for the actual quantification, and a drop in peroxidase-like activity as a built-in cross-check. The point is redundancy, so one flaky signal doesn't fool you the way single-probe assays do.

original_title: Bioorthogonal Tethering of FGF18 to Annealed Microgel Scaffolds Enhances Cartilage Repair
title: Giving FGF18 a fixed address in a cartilage scaffold
blurb: Recombinant FGF18 already improves cartilage thickness in trials, but only with high doses and repeat injections. Here it's tethered bioorthogonally to annealed PEG microgel scaffolds instead of injected free, the idea being to keep the growth factor parked where it's needed instead of dosing around it.

original_title: Assembly-formed bioorthogonal chimeric artificial receptors enable high-contrast fluorescence imaging of tumors
title: Self-assembling receptors that light tumors up against the background
blurb: Chimeric artificial receptors that self-assemble on tumor cells through bioorthogonal chemistry, built to deliver high-contrast fluorescence imaging of the tumor.

original_title: An Integrated Bio‐Based Film With Dynamic Covalent Networks for Coupled pH‐Responsive Release and Colorimetric Reporting
title: A film that changes color when it's actually releasing the drug
blurb: Quaternary ammonium chitosan and dialdehyde cellulose cross-linked via dynamic Schiff base chemistry, loaded with curcumin, so the film releases its cargo by pH and reports on itself with a color shift instead of needing a separate sensor. Curcumin also bumped tensile strength by about 60%, improved the barrier properties, and gave it real antioxidant activity by DPPH assay. A packaging film doubling as its own indicator.

original_title: Total Synthesis and Structural Confirmation of Curcusone I
title: Curcusone I's structure, confirmed by actually building it
blurb: The first asymmetric total synthesis of curcusone I confirms the structure that computational studies had already revised, settling it the hard way. The [5-7-6] tricyclic core it shares with daphnane and tigliane diterpenes gets built via a Rh-catalyzed selenium [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement cascade and a SmI2-mediated cyclization, with the oxabicyclo[3.2.1]octane framework assembled along the way. The computation called it right, and the route to prove it is a genuinely gnarly one.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Unnatural Amino Acid Substitutions to Improve In Vivo GRPR-Targeting Capability of [68Ga]Ga-SP01011 for Cancer Imaging
title: Patching the weak spots on a GRPR tracer with unnatural amino acids
blurb: [68Ga]Ga-SP01011 targets GRPR for cancer imaging but gets chewed up in vivo before it can finish the job. Swapping in unnatural amino acids at the likely cleavage sites is the fix being tested here, aiming for better stability without losing the high tumor uptake or low pancreatic uptake that made the original worth using.

original_title: Recycling 99 Tc From Nuclear Wastewater by Coupling Photocatalysis and In Situ Ion‐Exchange on Bifunctional K‐SnS/TiO 2 Heterojunction
title: Turning nuclear wastewater's Tc-99 problem into a Tc-99 supply
blurb: A bifunctional K-SnS/TiO2 heterojunction pairs photocatalysis with in-situ ion exchange to pull mobile 99TcO4- out of nuclear wastewater and lock it down as immobilized Tc3+, with formic acid helping generate the CO2- radicals on TiO2 that drive the reduction. Removal and recycling in one closed loop instead of just shoving the problem into a filter.

original_title: Catalytic StereochemicalRelay for the EnantioselectiveSynthesis of Acyclic Quaternary Stereocenters
title: Building a quaternary carbon exactly where you want it, off a ring
blurb: Acyclic quaternary stereocenters, especially the γ-quaternary kind sitting a few bonds from whatever's supposed to control them, are notoriously hard to set with any stereocontrol. This relies on a catalytic relay of [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangements to reorganize the framework while keeping that stereochemical fidelity intact, the kind of methods problem that matters more to total synthesis than it sounds like it should.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Antibody-Drug Conjugate Clears Residual Cancer in 70% of Leukemia Patients - Technology Networks
title: An ADC clearing residual leukemia in most patients treated
blurb: A 70% rate of clearing residual disease is a strong claim on an antibody-drug conjugate, but without knowing trial phase, patient count, or follow-up length, it's a headline number more than a result yet.

original_title: A novel scaling approach for human pharmacokinetic prediction of antibody-drug conjugates using minimal nonclinical data: Integration of monkey PK and in vitro data.
title: Predicting ADC pharmacokinetics in humans without the full nonclinical package
blurb: A scaling method that predicts human PK for antibody-drug conjugates from monkey PK plus in vitro data alone, skipping some of the usual nonclinical workup. Useful if it generalizes beyond whatever ADCs they validated it on.

original_title: Total Synthesis of Scytonemin and Reduced Scytonemin
title: A total synthesis of scytonemin, built from isatin and raspberry ketone
blurb: An intramolecular Mannich reaction stitches an aldol adduct of isatin and TIPS-protected raspberry ketone into a tricyclic half-scytonemin unit, which then dimerizes to the full skeleton. t-BuOCl installs the side-chain olefins regio- and stereoselectively in high yield, and DDQ closes out the scytonemin core in quantitative yield, with the reduced form reachable by simple interconversion.

original_title: Reverse DTNB assay: a novel in vitrobiochemical approach to detect oxidized thiol modifications
title: Flipping the DTNB assay around to catch oxidized thiols
blurb: Cysteine's SH/SSG/S-S/SNO interconversion makes oxidized thiol states a pain to pin down in living cells. This repurposes the standard DTNB reagent, run in reverse, to read out oxidized rather than free thiols, aiming to replace the slower conventional workarounds.

original_title: TLX591 Antibody-Based Lutetium-177 PSMA Therapy in Metastatic CRPC - Pedro Barata - UroToday
title: TLX591's antibody spin on Lu-177 PSMA therapy
blurb: Pedro Barata discusses TLX591, an antibody-based Lutetium-177 PSMA construct being tested in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.

original_title: Systematic Optimization of an SLE‐DAPTAD LC–MS/MS Workflow for Simultaneous Quantification of Low‐Abundance Vitamin D 3 Metabolites in Plasma
title: A cleaner LC-MS/MS workflow for the vitamin D metabolites everyone struggles to quantify
blurb: Vitamin D3 metabolites are structurally near-identical, matrix-bound, and ionize poorly, which makes low-abundance ones like 1,25(OH)2D3 especially rough to measure. Five sample-prep and derivatization strategies get systematically compared to land on a simplified workflow that quantifies 25(OH)D3, 3-epi-25(OH)D3, 1,25(OH)2D3, and 24,25(OH)2D3 in plasma all at once.

original_title: Structure-based redesign enables clinical translation of CAIX-targeted theranostics in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
title: Redesigning a CAIX-targeted theranostic to actually make it to clinic
blurb: A structure-based redesign of a CAIX-targeted theranostic agent for clear cell renal cell carcinoma, pitched as clinically translatable. Not much detail to go on beyond that.

original_title: The role of transglutaminase 2 in stabilizing fibrin clots and supporting hemostasis.
title: What transglutaminase 2 is doing to your fibrin clots
blurb: A look at how transglutaminase 2 cross-links and stabilizes fibrin clots to support normal hemostasis.

original_title: Theranostic Approach Using Radioiodinated Trimethoprim Targeting E. coli Dihydrofolate Reductase in Engineered Cells
title: Radioiodinated trimethoprim as a tag for E. coli DHFR-expressing cells
blurb: Trimethoprim binds bacterial, not human, dihydrofolate reductase, so a radioiodinated version makes a clean reporter for engineered cells carrying E. coli DHFR, with theranostic use in mind.

original_title: An Exogenous Base-Free Cu-Catalyzed Multicomponent Synthesis of 1,1-Aminoboranes from Alkylamines and Aldehydes
title: A Cu-catalyzed route to 1,1-aminoboranes that skips the base and the column
blurb: Aldehydes, alkylamines, and B2pin2 combine under Cu catalysis with no exogenous base needed, giving 1,1-amino(pinacol)boranes isolable as bench-stable HCl salts or neutral compounds without chromatography. It reaches secondary alkylamines that conventional Cu-catalyzed borylation of electron-deficient imines can't touch, which is the actual point.

original_title: Construction of novel phycocyanin conjugated chitosan–TiO2–Fe3O4 nanoparticles for Lactobacillus retainment and application in cyclic batch fermentation
title: Magnetic nanoparticles for fishing Lactobacillus back out of the fermenter
blurb: Chitosan-coated, phycocyanin-conjugated TiO2/Fe3O4 nanoparticles are built to stick to Lactobacillus cells so they can be pulled out magnetically between batch fermentation runs, aimed at industries that keep losing their starter culture to filtration-heavy downstream processing.

original_title: Preparation of different immobilized/stabilized biocatalyst of Alcalase by modification with glutaraldehyde.
title: Pinning Alcalase down with glutaraldehyde, several ways
blurb: Alcalase, the usual workhorse protease, crosslinked with glutaraldehyde into a handful of different immobilized and stabilized formats. Reads as a methods comparison rather than a result.

original_title: Construction of CF 2 moieties in FDA-approved drugs (2016–2025): industrial routes, mechanisms, and scale-up considerations
title: Twelve FDA drugs, one recurring problem: installing a CF2 group at scale
blurb: A review walking through the industrial routes behind 12 FDA-approved drugs carrying a CF2 unit, sorted by what it's attached to (alkyl, heteroaryl, or an aryl ether), plus why the routes that didn't make it to plant scale got dropped. Useful if you're the one stuck building difluoromethylenes at kilogram scale rather than on a bench.

original_title: Controlling Nickel Catalyst Reactivity by Controlling Molecular Catalyst Speciation
title: Keeping nickel catalysts from finding each other
blurb: Molecular Ni catalysts bolted to metal-oxide supports through a series of different anchoring groups, to see which one actually stops them dimerizing and dying over the course of a reaction. The anchor chemistry itself is the variable, not just a mounting detail.

original_title: Halogen Bonding as a Molecular Recognition Strategy for Genetic Code Expansion
title: Getting tRNA synthetases to spot an amino acid by its halogen, not its shape
blurb: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases usually need a dedicated binding pocket per amino acid, but this proposes they can pick out halogenated non-canonical amino acids through halogen bonding instead, a recognition handle beyond the usual shape-fit pocket, useful for genetic code expansion.

original_title: PSMA-targeting hybrid molecule PSMA-914 for preoperative imaging and intraoperative fluorescence-guidance: A first-in-human experience.
title: One PSMA probe for the scan and the scalpel
blurb: First-in-human data on PSMA-914, a hybrid PSMA-targeting molecule built to do preoperative imaging and then switch to intraoperative fluorescence guidance in the same patient, one compound instead of swapping agents between the scan and the surgery.

original_title: Shape‐Complementary DNA Scaffold for Programmable Functionalization of Symmetric Protein Assemblies
title: Using a DNA scaffold as a jig to decorate protein rings
blurb: A shape-complementary DNA nanostructure that controls how many streptavidin-DNA conjugates get loaded onto symmetric protein assemblies, shown by transferring them off a ring-shaped DNA scaffold onto a recombinant tobacco mosaic virus disk. The point is dialing in valency and spacing on purpose instead of taking whatever stoichiometry the chemistry hands you.

original_title: Redox-Active Ligand-Assisted Ruthenium-Catalyzed Lemieux–Johnson-Type Oxidation of Olefins for Aldehyde Synthesis
title: A ruthenium catalyst that knows when to stop cleaving
blurb: Redox-active ligands act as an electron reservoir, cycling the Ru center through Ru(V)=O/Ru(VI) species to cleave C=C bonds into aldehydes, while the same ligand's steric bulk keeps those aldehydes from over-oxidizing into carboxylic acids. Runs at room temperature in ethyl acetate, with the ligand pulling double duty as electron buffer and guard rail.

original_title: A Unified Analytical Framework for LYSO-SiPM Scintillation Pulse Dynamics
title: One model for the whole LYSO-SiPM signal chain instead of four separate ones
blurb: Scintillation kinetics, optical transport, SiPM response, and timing statistics are normally modeled separately; this stitches them into a single forward model, complete with thermalization delay, depth-dependent transit-time spread, and microcell occupancy effects, so the waveform gets predicted end to end instead of piece by piece.

original_title: Solvent/Base-Cocontrolled Regiodivergent Synthesis of 5-Arylnaphtho[1′,2′:4,5]imidazo[1,2- a ]pyridines and 3-Substituted 2-Arylimidazo[1,2- a ]pyridines from 2-Arylimidazo[1,2- a ]pyridines and α-Cl Ketones via a Rh(III)-Catalyzed C–H Activation Strategy
title: Same starting materials, and the solvent decides which product you get
blurb: Rh(III)-catalyzed C-H activation on 2-arylimidazo[1,2-a]pyridines with alpha-Cl ketones: run it in HFIP with K2CO3 and you get the fused naphtho-annulated product, swap to p-xylene with NaOAc and it stops instead at C3-H functionalization. Same catalyst, same substrates, solvent and base alone steer which ring system comes out, over a reportedly wide substrate scope.

original_title: A General Design of Compact “Zero‐On” NIR‐II Photoacoustic Dyes for High‐Fidelity Imaging
title: Small dyes that stay quiet until a biomarker flips them on
blurb: A general building-block design for compact NIR-II photoacoustic dyes built around a dimethyl-dihydroacridine core, made in three steps, that stay in a 'zero' state until a biomarker-responsive block switches on the signal. Keeping the molecular weight down while still getting a clean on/off jump is the part most probe designs don't pull off together.

original_title: Photon-Driven Catalytic Formic Acid Dehydrogenation Beyond the Sabatier Limit
title: Light gets platinum catalysts past the Sabatier limit
blurb: Sabatier scaling ties reactant activation, intermediate stability, and desorption together so tightly it caps how good a catalyst can be. Here 450 nm photons hit Pt during formic acid decomposition and selectively strip off the rate-limiting surface intermediate without touching the thermal energetics at all, boosting turnover 4000x, reversibly, isothermally. One substrate and one metal so far, but that's a genuinely different lever than swapping catalysts.

original_title: Trop2-targeted PET/CT imaging with (68)Ga-MY6349 improves diagnostic accuracy and influences clinical management in breast cancer.
title: A Trop2 PET tracer for breast cancer that apparently changes what doctors do
blurb: 68Ga-MY6349 targets Trop2 for PET/CT imaging in breast cancer and, per the report, improves diagnostic accuracy and actually shifts clinical management decisions. No numbers to go on beyond that claim.

original_title: Enantiodivergent Carbon–Phosphorus Bond Formation via Enzymatic Carbene Insertion
title: An enzyme that finally makes carbon-phosphorus bonds, and picks which mirror image
blurb: Phosphorus is one of the six elements of life but enzymes almost never build C-P bonds directly, which is awkward given how much P-stereogenic P(V) chemistry matters in drugs and agrochemicals where the configuration at phosphorus decides whether the thing works. This platform does direct enzymatic C-P bond formation via carbene insertion and is enantiodivergent, so you choose the stereochemistry rather than take what you get.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Patient Survival and Its Relation to Tumor Absorbed Dose in [(177)Lu]Lu-DOTATATE Therapy of Neuroendocrine Tumors.
title: Tumor dose, not just injected dose, tracks survival on Lu-177-DOTATATE
blurb: A look at whether the radiation dose actually absorbed by neuroendocrine tumors during Lu-177-DOTATATE therapy correlates with how long patients survive, rather than just the amount infused. No effect sizes given, but dosimetry-as-predictor is the point.

original_title: Shape‐Complementary DNA Scaffold for Programmable Functionalization of Symmetric Protein Assemblies
title: A DNA scaffold that hands proteins off one at a time
blurb: A shape-matched DNA nanostructure used to control valency on symmetric protein assemblies rather than the usual all-or-nothing labeling. They show streptavidin-DNA conjugates transferring in a controlled way off a ring-shaped DNA scaffold onto a recombinant tobacco mosaic virus disk, essentially programming how many copies land and where.

original_title: Programmed S → N Remote Cyano Migration: A Thiocyanate-Based Entry to Cyanamides and Selective Ferroptosis Inducers
title: Cheap thiocyanate opens a route to cyanamide ferroptosis drugs
blurb: Ferroptosis is one of the few ways around apoptosis-resistant tumors, but cyanamide scaffolds, a good chemical space for inducing it, have been blocked by how hard the N-CN bond is to build. This cascade cyclization uses inorganic thiocyanate, cheap and low-toxicity, as an electrophilic CN surrogate that migrates the cyano group from sulfur to nitrogen, delivering cyanamides including some selective ferroptosis inducers.

original_title: One-step selective synthesis of benzofuran or hydroxyacetophenone derivatives with potential anticancer activity
title: One reaction, two different anticancer scaffolds depending how you run it
blurb: A one-step synthesis that can be steered selectively toward either benzofuran or hydroxyacetophenone derivatives, both flagged for anticancer activity. No potency data given, just the route.

original_title: Reprogramming ω -Transaminase for Enantioselective Assembly of Axially Chiral Spiro[3.3]heptane Building Blocks
title: An engineered transaminase builds axially chiral spiro amines directly
blurb: Axially chiral amines on spiro[3.3]heptane scaffolds are useful in med chem but making them by direct asymmetric amination of the hindered ketone was basically off the table. Starting from a weak wild-type omega-transaminase out of Arthrobacter sp. KNK168, they engineered a double variant that does the amination directly on 2,6-disubstituted spiro[3.3]heptanones in water, under mild conditions.

original_title: Universal Metal-Free Deborylation–Deuteration via Redox-Decoupled Tandem Flow Electrosynthesis
title: Splitting a flow cell's two reactions so deuteration doesn't fight itself
blurb: Flow electrochemistry is a good way to make deuterium-labeled compounds, but it usually gets bottlenecked by a counter half-reaction that doesn't match what you actually want happening. This decouples deborylation and deuteration into separate sequential electrochemical steps in one tandem flow cell, and reports metal-free, universal deuteration across a broad set of organoboron substrates.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Unsaturated Copper Sites for Selective Electroreduction of CO to Alcohol
title: Undercoordinated copper pushes CO reduction toward alcohol instead of just any C2+ product
blurb: CO electroreduction is already good at C2+ selectivity in general, but alcohol specifically has lagged on both selectivity and energy efficiency. Reducing Cu2O with ammonia leaves low-coordination Cu sites that bind CO more tightly and favor pre-protonating it to *CHO rather than letting two CO molecules couple, which is what tilts the output toward alcohol instead of the usual C2+ grab bag.

original_title: Membranolytic peptide programs immunogenic cell death for cancer therapy
title: A peptide that only pops open in tumor-acidic turf
blurb: aMPC16-CA50 is a synthetic membranolytic peptide tuned to activate at tumor pH, and the way it lyses cancer cells counts as immunogenic cell death rather than just killing them quietly. That immune-priming effect is what lets it meaningfully boost checkpoint blockade instead of just adding another cytotoxic mechanism.

original_title: Replicating the Bohr/Haldane effect in a synthetic system
title: Hemoglobin's O2/CO2 crosstalk, built into a synthetic system
blurb: The Bohr and Haldane effects are the allosteric coupling that lets hemoglobin trade oxygen binding against CO2 and proton binding depending on where it's sitting in the body. This gets that same coupling working outside a cell, in a synthetic system.

original_title: Time-Resolved Polymorphism in a Cd-MOF with Dual Applications in Iodine Adsorption and One-Pot Tandem Knoevenagel–Michael Cyclocondensation Catalysis
title: Same Cd-MOF ligands, two different frameworks, just a matter of timing
blurb: MOF-J and MOF-A come out of the same solvothermal synthesis with identical ligands, but crystallization time decides which polymorph forms, with monoclinic MOF-J as the kinetically favored product. Both do double duty as iodine adsorbents and catalysts for one-pot Knoevenagel-Michael cyclocondensations.

original_title: Boraindenes as versatile precursors to benzannulated boron heterocycles
title: Boraindenes as the missing middle child of boron heterocycles
blurb: Boraindenes slot in as a bicyclic starting point for benzannulated boron heterocycles, sitting between the monocyclic boroles and the tricyclic 9-borafluorenes as versatile precursors. More of a synthetic on-ramp than a destination itself.

original_title: Ultrasound-Driven Reductive Deoxygenation of N -Oxides for Spatiotemporally Controlled Prodrug Activation
title: Switching on a tumor prodrug with an ultrasound wand
blurb: N-oxide prodrugs usually need a tumor's own hypoxic or reductive chemistry to activate, which is inconsistent. Here clinical ultrasound (1 MHz) drives a riboflavin tetrabutyrate/NADPH redox relay that cleaves the N-O bond directly via electron and hydrogen-atom transfer, so activation happens wherever the transducer points rather than wherever the tumor cooperates.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Vimentin remodeling in response to oxidants and electrophiles is modulated by pH.
title: Vimentin's oxidative stress response comes with a pH dial
blurb: Oxidants and electrophiles remodel the intermediate filament protein vimentin, and pH turns out to modulate how that remodeling proceeds.

original_title: Synthesis of Unsymmetrically 1,3,5-Trisubstituted Arenes via Site-Selective Sequential Silylation and Borylation
title: An iridium catalyst that picks arene sites by shape, not electronics
blurb: A spirobipyridine ligand with a steric roof lets an iridium catalyst site-selectively silylate and borylate monosubstituted arenes regardless of their electronics, and it works in either order. The product carries both a boron and a silicon handle, so it's really a modular gateway to unsymmetrical 1,3,5-trisubstituted arenes rather than a finished product.

original_title: Skeletal Editing of α-Oxoketene- N , S -Acetals into Amides via Cooperative Base-Promoted/Copper-Catalyzed Amidation
title: Building amides by kicking a thiol out of a ketene acetal first
blurb: Base eliminates MeSH from an α-oxoketene-N,S-acetal to give a ketenimine, which hydrates to an enolic amide that coordinates Cu(OAc)2 and then rearranges through a 1,3-arylamine shift into the final secondary amide, with DFT backing up the mechanism. A roundabout route to amides, but a fairly practical one that skips the usual acid-amine coupling.

original_title: Controlled Aryl-to-Alkyl Amide Migration Enables Access to Structurally Diversified Antiviral Quinolines
title: Migrating an amide from the ring to the alkyl chain on quinolines
blurb: Quinoline and quinazoline cores are everywhere in drugs, but shuffling substituents around the aromatic ring without rebuilding it from scratch has stayed mostly unexplored. This is an in situ amide that migrates intramolecularly from an aryl to an alkyl position, opening a route to structurally diverse antiviral quinolines without de novo synthesis.

original_title: Hematologic Consequences of Radiopharmaceutical Therapy: From Clonal Hematopoiesis to Therapy-Related Myeloid Neoplasms.
title: What radiopharmaceutical therapy does to your bone marrow, eventually
blurb: A review tracking the hematologic fallout of radiopharmaceutical therapy, from clonal hematopoiesis up through full therapy-related myeloid neoplasms. The kind of long-tail toxicity that's easy to lose track of when everyone's watching the tumor response numbers.

original_title: Patient Survival and Its Relation to Tumor Absorbed Dose in [ 177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE Therapy of Neuroendocrine Tumors
title: Does hitting your Lu-177 dose target actually predict survival
blurb: A dosimetry study tying how much radiation the tumor actually absorbed during Lu-177-DOTATATE therapy to how long neuroendocrine tumor patients survived afterward, the kind of dose-outcome link PRRT dosimetry has mostly been arguing for on theory.

original_title: Copper-Catalyzed Enantioselective Vinylogous Hydroxylation with Nitrosobenzene
title: Copper cracks vinylogous hydroxylation's selectivity problem
blurb: Vinylogous hydroxylation has stayed mostly unclaimed territory because the oxygen donors that could do it tend to over-oxidize and wreck both regio- and enantioselectivity. Here nitrosobenzene runs an enantioselective vinylogous nitroso aldol addition first, and copper cleaves the N–O bond afterward to reveal the alcohol, sidestepping the oxidant problem instead of solving it head-on.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Photoredox‐Catalyzed Cyclopropane Ring‐Opening: A Metal‐Free and Sustainable Strategy
title: Cyclopropane ring-opening, no metal required
blurb: Organic photoredox catalysts swapped in for the usual metal photocatalysts to pry open strained cyclopropane rings under visible light, sold as the greener, milder route to the same ring-opened products people already use these strained intermediates for.

original_title: Reactivity and Improved Synthesis of Tetrafluoroargentate Salts
title: A bench-safe route to AgF4-, the scary +III silver oxidant
blurb: [AgF4]- is a serious oxidizer with silver parked in the rare +III state, but making it used to mean handling elemental fluorine and anhydrous HF. This swaps that for just stirring AgF2 with a tetraalkylammonium halide or FPPh4 in acetonitrile: silver disproportionates and hands over [NR4][AgF4] or [PPh4][AgF4] plus the silver halide byproduct, on preparative scale, no F2 required.

original_title: Photoinduced Synthesis of 5-Amino-1,2,4-Thiadiazoles from Amidines and Isothiocyanates
title: Thiadiazoles built with light and no photocatalyst
blurb: Benzamidine hydrochlorides and isothiocyanates cascade into 5-amino-1,2,4-thiadiazoles via C–N/N–S bond formation, and light alone does the oxidizing, no photocatalyst added. Radical trapping and UV–vis point to a sulfur-centered radical off an in-situ thiolate as the key step, with a scope the authors call broad and functional-group tolerant.

original_title: Engineering Oxygen Vacancy Densities on (002)-Faceted ZnO Nanoplates: Tunable Adsorption Selectivity between CO2 and C2H6 for Efficient Ethylene Production
title: Tuning ZnO defects to pick CO2 or ethane out of the mix
blurb: CO2-assisted oxidative dehydrogenation of ethane could turn CO2 and ethane into ethylene together, but activating a C–H and a C=O bond at once without coking the catalyst has been the holdup. Oxygen vacancy density on (002)-faceted ZnO nanoplates turns out to control which gas adsorbs at all: low vacancy density favors CO2, high density flips it over to ethane. A defect knob for a selectivity problem that's usually just a tradeoff.

original_title: Two Reactivities for the Price of One Cycle: Sulfonamides as Dual Photoinduced Electron Transfer/Hydrogen Atom Transfer Catalysts
title: One catalyst cycle doing two different jobs
blurb: Cyclic biaryl sulfonamides (BASNs) normally just run photoinduced electron transfer, but the nitrogen-centered radical left behind after PET can turn around and do hydrogen atom transfer on a second substrate, squeezing two reactivities out of one cycle. They demonstrate it by reductively activating gem-difluoroalkenes and using that same intermediate for the HAT step. Neat if it generalizes past this substrate pairing.

original_title: Scalable Synthesis of a Masked Thiophenol as an Air-Stable, Odorless Intermediate to the Aurora Kinase Inhibitor Tozasertib (VX-680)
title: A kinase-inhibitor intermediate without the thiophenol stench
blurb: Thiophenols are toxic, reek, and fall apart in air, a real problem when you need one at process scale for the Aurora kinase inhibitor tozasertib (VX-680). The workaround is Ni-catalyzed C–S coupling of aryl iodides with thiourea to give an S-aryl isothiouronium salt, a crystalline, odorless, bench-stable thiophenol stand-in unmasked later in the route. This is the process-scale version of that trick, with catalyst loading pushed down to 0.5 mol %.

original_title: Photoredox-Catalyzed Radical Hexafluoroisopropoxylation of Arenes and Heteroarenes
title: Bolting a hexafluoroisopropoxy group straight onto C–H bonds
blurb: The hexafluoroisopropoxy group has the lipophilic and electronic properties people want but barely gets used because it's a pain to install. A bench-stable N-hexafluoroisopropoxy benzotriazole serves as the radical precursor here, hitting arene and heteroarene C–H bonds directly under visible light, mild conditions, and reportedly a scope that reaches into pharma-relevant heterocycles.

original_title: Rational design, synthesis, and evaluation of acridone–peptide based antimicrobial and Antifolate agents against methicilin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, Bacillus subtilis and dihydrofolate reductase
title: Acridone-peptide hybrids going after MRSA and DHFR at once
blurb: Acridone-peptide conjugates designed to hit MRSA and Bacillus subtilis directly while also blocking dihydrofolate reductase, folding an antifolate mechanism into the same antimicrobial scaffold rather than treating the two as separate drugs.

original_title: Electrocatalytic C–C Coupled Oligomerization From Biomass Molecules Through Pd Single‐Atom Interfacial Regulation
title: Trimerizing biomass molecules electrochemically, past the dimer wall
blurb: Electrocatalytic C-C coupling of biomass molecules has been stuck making dimers. A Pd1Cu single-atom alloy catalyst pushes it further, giving a trimer of HMF (5-hydroxymethylfurfural) at 44.7% selectivity. One step toward diesel-range fuel from biomass instead of food crops, though the hydrodeoxygenation upgrading step still has to follow.

original_title: Site-specific and global glycan analysis of the human cytomegalovirus pentameric glycoprotein by high resolution mass spectrometry
title: Mapping the glycans on HCMV's vaccine antigen of choice
blurb: High-resolution mass spec maps the site-specific and global glycosylation of the HCMV pentamer complex, the glycoprotein target behind the more potent neutralizing vaccine candidates. Heavy glycosylation is one suspect for why antibody responses to it are often weak, so knowing exactly where the sugars sit matters for design.

original_title: Bioinspired Large-Area Polymeric Cucurbituril Monolayers with Ultrahigh-Density Nanopores Enabling Reversible Charge-Gating of Ion Transport via Host–Guest Recognition
title: Subnanometer pores that gate ions on command, at wafer scale
blurb: Cucurbituril host-guest complexes get cross-linked into 2D amorphous membranes up to 900 cm2, with subnanometer channels whose amphiphilicity can be tuned so the pores gate ion transport reversibly via host-guest recognition, active gating rather than just size sieving. Getting that kind of control at wafer scale, not just a few-micron flake, is the actual selling point here.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Bifunctional (Al)TS-1 Prepared by Sequential Insertion of Active Sites for Ethylene to Glycol
title: Getting Al and Ti to stop competing for the same zeolite sites
blurb: Inserting Al into TS-1 after the fact, via hydrothermal post-treatment, rather than co-crystallizing both metals together sidesteps the competitive insertion between Al and Ti that usually plagues Al-TS-1 synthesis. The result is a bifunctional zeolite with both acid and oxidation sites for turning ethylene into glycol, with morphology and activity tunable through the post-treatment solution's composition.

original_title: Interfacial Raft‐Like Structures From Bottlebrush Polymers
title: Bottlebrush polymers form rafts at an interface, then block their own neighbors
blurb: Amphiphilic random-copolymer-grafted bottlebrushes, made by copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition, settle at a fluid-fluid interface as laterally confined 'raft' structures with their side chains lying parallel to it. Each raft leaves a bare patch of interface that other rafts can't adsorb into, so the polymers end up capping their own packing density instead of maximizing it.

original_title: An isotope dilution-liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry-based candidate reference measurement procedure for the quantification of meropenem in human serum and plasma
title: A reference-grade way to actually trust your meropenem levels
blurb: An isotope-dilution LC-MS/MS candidate reference measurement procedure for meropenem in serum and plasma, with the standard characterized by quantitative NMR to keep it metrologically traceable to the international system. Not exciting chemistry, but the kind of paper that lets every hospital's meropenem TDM assay get checked against the same yardstick.

original_title: Acylation of N -Heteroarenes with Aldehydes Catalyzed by Photoexcited Hydrogen Chloride in Acetonitrile
title: Photoexcited HCl doing acylation chemistry that usually needs something fancier
blurb: Plain hydrogen chloride in acetonitrile, excited with light, is the whole catalyst system here, driving acylation of six classes of N-heteroarenes with both aromatic and aliphatic aldehydes. It's mild and fast, and about as cheap a catalyst as chemistry gets these days.

original_title: Radical-Mediated γ-C(sp3)−H Functionalization of Quaternary Ammonium Salts
title: A radical shortcut to the C-H bond quaternary ammoniums keep out of reach
blurb: Quaternary ammonium salts have no lone pair to anchor a directing group and their nearby C-H bonds are electronically deactivated, so they've mostly been left out of C-H functionalization chemistry. This generates alpha-ammonioalkyl radicals in situ that do an intramolecular hydrogen abstraction and land on the remote gamma C-H bond instead, with a traceless strategy and broad substrate scope claimed.

original_title: Real-Time Scanning Ion Conductance Microscopy Reveals MARCKS-Driven Morphological Remodeling and Nanomechanical Softening during LPS-Induced Macrophage Polarization
title: Watching a macrophage soften in real time as it polarizes
blurb: Scanning ion conductance microscopy tracks live nanomechanical and morphological changes in macrophages as LPS pushes them toward an inflammatory state, catching MARCKS-driven remodeling and a softening of the cell as it polarizes. Physical readouts of immune activation you'd otherwise only infer from biochemistry.

original_title: Structure-based macrocyclization of α-ketoamides leads to potent inhibitors of coronaviral and enteroviral proteases
title: Locking a coronavirus protease inhibitor into its bioactive shape with a macrocycle
blurb: Co-crystal structures of SARS-CoV-2 Mpro with peptidomimetic inhibitors showed side chains filling the S1'/S2 and S3/S1 pockets sitting close together, so they macrocyclized those pairs to rigidify the molecule. Two series came out of it: exocyclic nitriles bridging P3 and P1, and endocyclic alpha-ketoamides bridging P1' and P2, aimed at both coronaviral and enteroviral proteases at once.

original_title: Design and Elucidation of a Strain-Relief-Driven Ring Opening Mechanism of Inactivation of Ornithine Aminotransferase by (1 S ,3 R ,5 R )-3-Amino-6,6-difluorobicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-1-carboxylic Acid
title: A cyclopropane-fused inhibitor that inactivates hOAT by popping its own ring open
blurb: A difluorinated bicyclic amino acid knocks out human ornithine aminotransferase, the PLP enzyme hepatocellular carcinoma leans on for glutamine and proline synthesis. The ring strain is doing the work: once catalysis starts, that built-in tension drives the ring open and traps the enzyme for good. Mechanism-based inactivation engineered on purpose rather than stumbled into.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Metal-Anchored Silicon-Based Nanostructures Enable Dual-Polarity SALDI-MS Analysis of Small Molecules
title: Gold on silicon nanowires: one chip, both ionization modes
blurb: An ordered silicon nanowire array topped with gold nanoparticles (VSiNW-Au) works as a SALDI-MS substrate that ionizes small molecules in both positive and negative mode off the same chip, going after the reproducibility and throughput problems that usually sink these substrates. Worth something if the numbers hold past the reported panel.

original_title: Conserved copper(I)-binding auxiliary domains link virulence-associated LPMOs to copper homeostasis in the intestinal environment
title: Gut LPMOs come with their own copper-handling module
blurb: Virulence-linked LPMOs from intestinal pathogens carry conserved auxiliary domains that bind copper(I), tying these enzymes directly into how the bacteria manage copper in the gut rather than just chewing on host sugars. Builds on the CbpD story in Pseudomonas, where immunizing mice against a multidomain LPMO protected against lethal infection, so a copper-handling piece to that virulence puzzle is worth flagging.

original_title: Millisecond-Long Red Phosphorescence in Chiral Heteroleptic Ag(I) Complexes Bearing Benzothiazole Ligands
title: Chiral silver complexes that glow red for an unusually long time
blurb: Six chiral Ag(I) complexes pairing benzothiazole ligands with BINAP-family diphosphines phosphoresce orange-red with millisecond lifetimes, long for a coordination compound, off ligand-centered triplet states. Chirality and long-lived phosphorescence in the same molecule is the rarer combination here, not either property alone.

original_title: Quantitative dual-tracer 18F-FDG and 18F-DPA-714 PET/MR for characterizing pathological subtypes in refractory mesial temporal lobe epilepsy
title: Two PET tracers to sort out which kind of epilepsy you've got
blurb: Pairs 18F-FDG with the TSPO tracer 18F-DPA-714 on PET/MR to distinguish pathological subtypes of refractory mesial temporal lobe epilepsy, reading glucose metabolism and neuroinflammation together instead of picking one.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Topological Densification-Reinforced Robust and Durable Protein Adhesive at Dynamic Interfaces.
title: A protein glue built to survive interfaces that won't sit still
blurb: A protein-based adhesive built around topological densification, engineered to keep holding at interfaces that flex and shift instead of sitting still. Durability under motion is the whole pitch here.

original_title: Replicating the Palladium Structure Enables Ni3InN to Surpass Nickel in Selective Hydrogenation
title: Nickel that acts like palladium once you rebuild its structure
blurb: A nickel-indium-nitrogen antiperovskite (Ni3InN) copies palladium's catalytically relevant structure, and that mimicry is what boosts nickel's selectivity in hydrogenation. Indium plus subsurface nitrogen pull the d-band center down from -1.42 to -1.59 eV and stretch the Ni-Ni distance from 2.49 to 2.72 Å, closer to Pd's spacing. Cheap metal doing an expensive metal's job, if the structural mimicry is really what's carrying it.

original_title: Crystallinity-Dependent Reverse Hydrogen Spillover Governs Electrochemical CO2 Reduction to Methane
title: Crystallinity of the support decides whether your CO2 turns into methane
blurb: Cu-doped ZrO2 catalysts for electrochemical CO2 reduction show that the crystallinity of the ZrO2 support governs reverse hydrogen spillover, how active hydrogen migrates back off the copper, which in turn sets how much methane forms versus other reduction products. A structural knob for a step that's mostly been guessed at, on the support rather than the metal.

original_title: GPMAW Glyco-Search: An Integrated Workflow for Identification and Validation of Intact Sialylated N-Glycopeptides
title: A search workflow built for the glycopeptides everyone else's pipeline drops
blurb: GPMAW Glyco-Search pairs TiO2 enrichment with dual LC-MS/MS runs on both intact and deglycosylated glycopeptides, then IDs intact sialylated N-glycopeptides by high-accuracy mass mapping instead of a conventional database search. Sialylated glycopeptides are exactly the low-abundance, poorly fragmenting ones that slip through standard glycoproteomics search engines, so a workflow built around that specific failure mode is the point.

original_title: Redox-State-Driven Site Selectivity and Kinetic Gating in Polyoxovanadate Methylation
title: DFT says a vanadium cluster's redox state decides where it gets methylated
blurb: A computational study on the hexavanadate cluster [V6O13(TRIOLX)2]2- runs DFT and microkinetic modeling through successive methylation and reduction steps, and finds that electron count redistributes nucleophilicity across the cluster, setting both where methylation lands and how fast it goes. Redox state as a site-selectivity switch, on paper only since nobody's run this in a flask yet.

original_title: Synthesis of a 6,11- Dioxa Congener of Torgov’s Diene: A Platform Intermediate for Oxasteroid Discovery
title: A dioxa twist on Torgov's diene, built for oxasteroid hunting
blurb: De novo synthesis of a 6,11-dioxa version of Torgov's diene, the classic steroid-building intermediate, with two oxygens swapped into the ring via alkene isomerization off an advanced tetracycle. Gets there through a Schenck-ene photooxygenation, a cationic annulation, a singlet oxygen cascade, and a Pd2+ Friedel-Crafts cyclization, then branches into a set of saturated analogues via stereodivergent hydrogenation. Reads like a platform paper more than a target paper, the point is what people build from it next.

original_title: Backbone Steric Constraints Underlie High Passive Membrane Permeability of N ‐Alkyl Peptides
title: What actually makes N-alkyl peptides cross membranes
blurb: Removing the amide H is the standard explanation for why N-alkylated peptides permeate membranes, but this shows backbone sterics do real work too: substituting both the amide nitrogen and the alpha-carbon boosts passive permeability beyond what N-alkyl glycines, which lack the alpha substitution, manage on their own. Comparing the two side by side isolates the steric effect from the H-bonding one.

original_title: Topological Densification‐Reinforced Robust and Durable Protein Adhesive at Dynamic Interfaces
title: A protein glue that holds up against blood flow
blurb: An engineered lysine-rich elastin-like protein crosslinked with a star-shaped ortho-phthalaldehyde linker, dense and fast-bonding enough to seal tissue and stop bleeding even under high-velocity blood flow, where typical two-component biomimetic adhesives tend to give out. The trick is a topological densification strategy rather than a new chemistry, just tighter packing of the same covalent bonds.

original_title: Engineering a Highly meta -Selective Biphenyl Monooxygenase for the Biosynthesis of High-Value Polymer Precursors
title: Retooling a toluene monooxygenase to hit biphenyl in the meta position
blurb: Meta-hydroxylation without a directing group is normally a pain. Here, toluene/o-xylene monooxygenase gets re-engineered so distinct variants position biphenyl in the active site for sequential meta-selective hydroxylation, producing 3,3'-dihydroxybiphenyl, an industrial precursor to high-performance polymers, straight out of an enzyme instead of a synthetic route.

original_title: Lipophilic Salts of High Melting Point Drugs Modulate Solid-State Properties and Organic Solubility to Enable Manufacturability of Amorphous Solid Dispersions
title: Picking the right counterion to make amorphous drugs manufacturable
blurb: High melting point kills hot-melt extrusion and low organic solubility chokes spray-drying throughput, the two failure modes for amorphous solid dispersions. Nine lipophilic salts of atazanavir and mebendazole, paired with sulfate and sulfonate counterions across a range of chain lengths and bulk, show that counterion choice alone can shift a drug's Tm and solubility enough to reopen both manufacturing routes.

original_title: Bulk Stoichiometry-Controlled Surface Reconstruction of Nanosized Ni−In Intermetallic Catalysts Steers Methanol Selectivity in CO2 Hydrogenation
title: Stoichiometry decides which face a Ni-In catalyst shows CO2
blurb: SiO2-supported Ni-In intermetallic catalysts reconstruct their surfaces under CO2 hydrogenation conditions, and which way they reconstruct tracks the bulk Ni:In ratio, with certain compositions steering the surface toward methanol rather than the usual CO or hydrocarbon products. Bulk composition as a design lever on surface chemistry, not just something you measure after the fact.

original_title: Independent and Efficient Pyridone Scaffold: Universal Afterglow Chemiluminescence Platform for High-Contrast Bioimaging
title: One pyridone scaffold, no partner molecule, for afterglow imaging
blurb: Afterglow chemiluminescence imaging skips real-time excitation light and cuts phototoxicity, but the usual designs either burn through substrate irreversibly or lose signal to blue-shifted emission and sloppy energy transfer, especially in two-component hybrid systems. This pyridone scaffold does the whole job as one self-sufficient molecule, sidestepping those failure modes for high-contrast bioimaging.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Characterizing the Assembly and Functional Properties of Gene-Length Mixed DNA Monolayers on Electrodes for Cell-Free Expression
title: Gold electrodes that keep genes on hand for cell-free protein expression
blurb: Thiol-anchored, gene-length DNA monolayers on planar gold electrodes, with surface density tunable just by changing DNA concentration during incubation. The immobilized sfGFP genes drive cell-free protein expression straight off the electrode, pitched as a reusable template for bioelectronic and cell-free synthetic biology setups.

original_title: Approach to the New Anti- Staphylococcus aureus Agents Discovery from Isatine
title: Isatin-derived oxindoles that actually kill Staph
blurb: A set of 3-hydroxy-2-oxindoles and their alpha,beta-unsaturated analogues, built off isatin via straightforward aldol condensation, screened against Staphylococcus aureus. Several hit 73.9-100% growth inhibition at just 10 µM in the primary screen, a solid hit rate for a first-pass phenotypic screen.

original_title: Chemical modification in genetically encoded (poly)peptide display technologies
title: What chemistry does once display technology finds your peptide
blurb: A review on chemical modification layered onto genetically encoded display platforms, phage, mRNA, cell surface, the methods that couple genotype to phenotype for high-throughput peptide and protein discovery. The focus is on what gets bolted on chemically after the genetic encoding does the finding.

original_title: Charting the small-molecule universe from mass spectra with neuro-symbolic AI
title: Reading unknown mass spectra without a reference library to match against
blurb: AIMe pairs neural nets with symbolic reasoning to turn an unidentified spectrum into a structural annotation across the known chemical space, instead of just matching against reference libraries that only cover a sliver of it. Most small molecules mass spec turns up still don't have names, so scaling past library lookups is the actual target here.
